definition: A physical trade requires an actual delivery or receipt of the underlying commodity (e.g., barrels of crude); a financial trade settles purely in cash with no physical movement of the commodity.
core_idea: Energy markets split trades into physical and financial types because commodities like oil and gas are hard to transport and store, making physical settlement a distinct and more operationally demanding activity than pure cash settlement.
key_points: Physical contracts transfer ownership of an actual commodity between parties.
Financial contracts transfer only cash and let investors get price exposure without ever handling the commodity.
The author states physical trading is both more complex and potentially more financially rewarding than financial trading.
relationships: Physical trading complexity is a major driver of arbitrage opportunities described later in the chunk (operational risk substituting for financial risk).
trading_implications: Traders who are equipped to handle physical logistics (e.g., taking delivery) can access profit opportunities that pure financial traders cannot.
caveats: It would be a mistake to focus only on financial markets since many of their features only make sense in light of underlying physical market mechanics.
